<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via validateRlsPredicateEnforceability (symbol, a top-level function), validateSharingRuleEnforceability (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c58008187fb14259cae52461aff9971a1b4b15e9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fe33964b711725635d55d4612605a7ba8a5fd488` — the merge of head `806dd06b0fe3f915f32a7b022d5f505166a0169d` into base `c58008187fb14259cae52461aff9971a1b4b15e9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fe33964b711725635d55d4612605a7ba8a5fd488 && git checkout fe33964b711725635d55d4612605a7ba8a5fd488
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c58008187fb14259cae52461aff9971a1b4b15e9 806dd06b0fe3f915f32a7b022d5f505166a0169d && git checkout -B drift-repro c58008187fb14259cae52461aff9971a1b4b15e9 && git merge --no-ff 806dd06b0fe3f915f32a7b022d5f505166a0169d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c58008187fb14259cae52461aff9971a1b4b15e9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c58008187fb14259cae52461aff9971a1b4b15e9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Per rule, the move is correct and each now accepts exactly the served name set, with one exception (item 2). Eight rules take `indexServedObjectGraph` (:510-512), which is `indexObjectGraph` over `objectsAsServed`, so the three skips, the injected columns and the `FieldPathVerdict` family are unchanged by construction; the four that keep a second index beside the graph (list-view option map :1071, widget field types :819, page field names :611-612, sharing anchor graph :580-596) build both from the same `served` array, so one rule cannot hold two accounts of an object. No finding-emitting line changed in any of the fourteen files (the diff is index swaps and comments), so rule id, severity, `where`, path and message of a true unknown are the same code path as before. The declared-only reads that remain are the right ones: the walks over what the stack OWNS (`validate-object-field-refs.ts` :507 own field lists, `validate-list-view-field-refs.ts` :1441 built-in list views, `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts` :1970 `defaultRowScope`, `validate-field-consumers.ts` :1257 the ledger) stay on `stack.objects` while resolution goes through the served graph, which is the per-package leg's own rule (`artifact-packages.ts` :182-186: resolution context changes what a rule can RESOLVE, never what it JUDGES). RLS: the graph answers existence and type for `judgeClause` / `judgePolicy` (:1942, :1953, :1976) and the membership trace (:1919); the runtime compiler reads the object's columns from the live `SchemaRegistry` (`rls-compiler.ts` :172-178), i.e. the merged definition, so a predicate on an extension-added field compiles and is enforced there, and lint's only prior verdict on it was a false `rls-predicate-unknown-field`; no ownership or anchor semantics read fields (`owner_id` is injected over the base layer, which the fold leaves alone, docblock :462-466). Sharing: the anchor arm reads `sharingModel` (:499) and `effectiveSharingModelOf`, neither of which the fold touches (only `fields` move, :497); `masterOf` (:405) now sees an extension-added `master_detail`, which changes only the hint's master name and matches the #23210 merge `validate-security-posture.ts` :748 already reads; the list-holding and cross-class arms judge the criteria filter the seeder compiles with the same `compileCelToFilter` call (`declared-sharing-rules.ts` :141) against the registry's object, and on an extension-added list-holding or cross-class field they now REFUSE where they were silent (unknowable), the strict direction. Neither rule needed to stay on declared fields; the dev's weighing in the body is right.
2. Must-fix, measured: `validate-related-list-refs.ts` now refuses a valid related list on the per-package leg. Head :139-141 lists every target of `objectExtensionsByTarget` that `objects` does not declare as a judged child carrying its extensions' fields alone; main :132-135 did the same only for the stack's TOP-LEVEL entries, which on the per-package leg (`packageBodyAsStack` :186, `objects` = this package's own, `packages[]` = every body) are this package's own. So a sibling package's extension of a child a third package owns now makes that child judged on fields that cannot hold its FK, and `judge` :180 refuses instead of skipping (`wholeCollection` is off on that leg, `reference-integrity-suite.ts` :441-443). Probe: packages `a` (owns `a_x`, `relatedLists: ['d_obj']`), `d` (owns `d_obj` with `x_id` lookup to `a_x`), `b` (extends `d_obj` with a text field); the per-package leg of `a` gives `related-list-ref-unknown` at head and nothing at main (Local-runs d); the union leg is clean on both. The runtime serves `d_obj` with its FK, so this is a false refusal at `error` on `os build`, on exactly the multi-package shape the card exists to admit, and the header line at :26-31 documents it as intended rather than weighing it. The pins do not reach it because every stack in the new describe is union-shaped (`artifact` :573-581 puts all three objects at the top level).
3. The two retired readers. Mapping (main `extensionFieldsByTarget`, top level plus every body, additive): the measured deltas are (a) top-level entries beside `packages[]` no longer read, a shape no CLI leg produces (the union repeats its bodies, `authoringRuleUnionStack` :356-392; the per-package leg carries the body's own entries in its `packages[]` entry too), and the old fixture that relied on it is rewritten to the two served shapes (:183-247, both parsed as the registry reads them); (b) one entry per package per target, pinned (:680-700). Related list (main: top level only, map-form `fields` only): (a) sibling bodies' extensions now seen, the card's defect, pinned (:670-684); (b) array-form `fields` now read, a widening (fewer refusals); (c) one entry per package, pinned; (d) the per-package-leg regression of item 2, unpinned. On (b) of both readers: `defineStack` refuses two `objectExtensions` entries for one target within a stack (`stack.zod.ts` :3198-3209 identity by `extend`, :3212-3240, top level only), so the replacement-versus-additive difference bites only on an input that door already refuses, in the refusing direction here. Showcase before/after identical as reported; not reproduced.
4. Pins. The nine-row `it.each` (:627-633) pins, per rule, an extension-added `ref_no` passing, the same stack with `objectExtensions: []` refusing (the non-vacuity control), and `nowhere` refused under the same id; the type arms (:643-667) pin a served-type verdict that an ablation cannot fake; field-consumers (:661-668) pins the credit and the no-finding-on-extension-fields property; both retired readers' replacement (:680-700). Real: the dev's ablation of the helper reddens the nine routed pins; my ablations of two direct readers redden exactly their own pin (Local-runs b, c), and by the same reading the other four direct readers' pins redden the same way. Gaps: (a) ids only; severity, `where` and message of the `nowhere` refusal are not compared against a declared-only control, so "same message" is by reading of the untouched emit sites, not pinned (PR #30359's test 3 pinned byte-equality); (b) no per-package-leg shape anywhere in the new describe, which is how item 2 escaped; (c) the type arms (`validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`, `validate-preset-comparands.ts`, the sharing cross-class arm) ignore `objectsAsServed(...).tied`, which the membership-key rule (:267) consults; a field two packages define at equal priority is judged on carrier order, which the fold docblock (:466-468) says a stack does not state. Narrow, unpinned.
5. Declarations and serial constraint. PR body and changeset carry `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none (lint judgements, no authorable key)`; `readMetadataProtocolLine` (:558-572) reads the first value token, so the parenthesis is tolerated; the changeset grades `@objectstack/lint` `patch`, the level `none` owes; `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are green on the head, `Test Core` (8 shards), `Build Core`, `Type Check` and `Lint` contexts still `in_progress`. `Prior rulings read:` line present (2 hits, ADR-0029 D3, ADR-0146 D10). #30270: this PR edits `validate-page-field-bindings.ts` at :125 (import) and :607-620; #30270 edits its header (:52), inserts `isPageSortRef` before the function (:600-615), and touches :643 and :690; `git merge-tree --write-tree pr-30432 pr-30270` produces a tree with no conflict, and the two changes are semantically independent (served index versus which sort refs the walk reads). #30270's base predates `ad0fbfd1`, and its `validate-sortable-fields.ts` :508 reads `recordsOf(stack.objects)`, so that rule's blind spot is measured, not "not measured" as the body says.
6. Body versus code. The per-rule table matches the diff and the pins row for row; the retired-reader notes match the measurement in item 3; "no rule stays on declared fields" is true; 384 changed lines and 17 `.ts` files are right. The three carried findings are real and correctly scoped out: (a) `validate-expressions.ts` `buildFieldIndex` (:202, :2231) and the `indexObjectFields` readers (`validate-react-page-props.ts` :1139, `validate-flow-node-writes.ts` :240, `validate-action-body-writes.ts` :382 all call the page rule's export, whose body :458-461 still reads `stack.objects`; `validate-hook-body-writes.ts` :505 is its own copy) index declared objects only, and this PR moved the page rule's CALL (:612) without moving the export, so the three siblings stay blind by design; (b) `validate-translation-references.ts` :1135-1152 keeps a third private fold (top level plus every body, every entry kept, and it reads validation rules the shared fold does not carry); (c) `stack.zod.ts` `collectRelatedListNameErrors` :4063-4100 folds every entry additively and reads every body's `objects`, so it differs from lint on the replaced-entry case (moot at the stack door, item 3) and, after the item 2 fix, should be the model lint follows for a child a sibling owns.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint` patch. Refusals narrow on the union leg (extension-added fields pass under fourteen rules); ids, severities and messages of a true unknown are unchanged by reading of the untouched emit sites. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are the right pair. The item 2 regression is a narrowing on the per-package leg that the fix removes; it does not change the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Lint still imports no runtime; every moved rule reads the one fold, and the fold is unchanged (`object-graph.ts` :417-500 byte-identical to `ad0fbfd1`; only :510-512 is new). The registry's short-name legacy-key fold (#28858) stays unmirrored, in the refusing direction, as PR #30359 recorded.
- The per-package leg is the boundary this PR did not test: `objectsAsServed` folds extensions onto `stack.objects` only, which is right for that leg's resolution rule, but any rule that ALSO lists `objectExtensionsByTarget` targets as judged subjects (today only the related-list rule, :139-141) turns a sibling's extension into a verdict on an object this package does not own.
- Carried tier: the `indexObjectFields` / `buildFieldIndex` family, the translation reader, `validate-sortable-fields.ts` (#30270's lane), and the `defineStack` twin; none security-rated in the accepting direction.

### ④ Design judgment

The shape is right: one helper beside the fold, every field-path rule resolving through it, the per-rule table honest about what each judges, and the two security rules weighed rather than exempted. Must-fix, in order: (1) `validate-related-list-refs.ts` :139-141: for a target `objects` does not declare, either leave it unjudged (drop the loop; on the union leg every declared target is already folded at :136-138, and a target no body declares is a platform object whose FK set this rule cannot know) or fold the sibling bodies' declared `objects` for it as `collectRelatedListNameErrors` does; rewrite the header line :26-31 to say which; pin it with a per-package-shaped stack (`objects` = one package's own, `packages[]` = every body, a sibling child a third package extends) that must be clean, plus the whole-collection control that a child nowhere is still refused. Should-fix, in order: (2) add one per-package-leg case to the `[#30383]` describe for the moved rules, the shape PR #30359's pins used, so the leg that ships is pinned too; (3) pin severity, `where` and message of the `nowhere` refusal byte-equal to a declared-only control for at least one rule per helper path; (4) consult `tied` in the three type arms, or state in each header that a tied definition is judged on package order; (5) correct the body's "whose index was not measured" for `validate-sortable-fields.ts` to "reads declared objects only (:508 at #30270's head)". Landing waits on (1) and on the running required contexts.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Must-fix of round 1, fixed. `validate-related-list-refs.ts` :139-141 now merges only `objectsAsServed(stack).objects`; the loop that listed every `objectExtensionsByTarget` target as a judged child is deleted and the `objectExtensionsByTarget` import is gone (:67). The header :26-35 now says which option was taken and why (the per-package leg holds one body's objects, so an extension alone is not a field set). The pin at `object-graph.test.ts` :692-701 is the per-package shape round 1 asked for (app body as the stack, `lib` owning `xs_note` and its FK, `mod` extending `xs_note` with `mood`, every body under `packages[]`) and must be clean; at `e27387e2` that stack produced `xs_note` in `fieldsByObject` with `mood` alone and `namedBy` empty, so the dev's "1 failed | 84 passed" ablation is what the reading gives.
